simple.meaning: טָפַח (ṭâphach) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to flatten out or extend (as a tent); figuratively, to nurse a child (as promotive of growth);.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Isaiah, Lamentations, beginning at Isaiah 48:13. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טָפַח (H2946) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: טָפַח (ṭâphach) / H2946 is traced through Isaiah 48:13, Lamentations 2:22 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to flatten out or extend (as a tent); figuratively, to nurse a child (as promotive of growth);
definitions.full: H2946. taphach [ טָפַח ] verb extend, spread (Arabic be full to overflowing, abound ; Aramaic extend, spread ; טְפוּחָא a step, foot-length ; Late Hebrew טֶפַח a span (compare טֶפַח below)) — Pi`el Perfect טִמְּחָה Isa 48:13 ; טִמַּחְתִּי Lam 2:22 ; — 1 spread out the heavens Isa 48:13 (|| ארץ יָסְדָה ). 2 denominative from טֶפַח carry on the palms, dandle Lam 2:22 (|| רִבִּיתִי I have brought up, reared ).
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; or perhaps a denominative from 2947 , from dandling on the palms
